text: The author's narrative style is characterized by a third-person omniscient point of view, as the narrator observes and comments on the detective's actions and demeanor from an external perspective. The tone is analytical and appreciative, highlighting the detective's "meticulous attention to detail" and "clinical detachment." The style itself is described as straightforward and objective, lacking embellishment, which mirrors the detective's own approach to the case. The sudden insertion of a factual question about seasons at the end serves as a jarring contrast to the otherwise serious and descriptive narrative tone.
